description:
Problem: .github/workflows/oracle-gate.yml schedules its sweep with cron '41 * * * *' (:35-36). The last 12 scheduled sweeps (2026-10-23T13:46Z to 2026-10-25T06:46Z) started 3 to 5 hours apart, for example 01:33Z then 06:46Z; GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs under load. The push trigger (:6-17) runs the sweep only when the gate's policy files change. Event-started gate runs are fast: across 100 non-sweep gate runs on 2026-10-24/25 the median and 90th-percentile queue wait was 0 s and the worst 21 minutes. So for the cases below the sweep cadence is the long pole:
(a) a gate run that cannot read the PR through REST or GraphQL posts nothing;
(b) a verdict post job that fails after posting its review but before its dispatch step, for verdict runs started by a comment, dispatch or schedule, whose completion the bridge cannot map;
(c) resolving the last oracle thread starts no Actions run, leaving a stale failure. Merge safety is held by the ruleset's thread-resolution rule; this is a delay, and oracle-review-automatic-reevaluation-20261021 owns the event side;
(d) the cancel-in-progress stranding cases recorded in oracle-review-automatic-reevaluation-20261021.

Outcome: a sweep backstop with a measured upper bound that does not depend on GitHub's cron cadence.

Decision gates:
1. Mechanism. Default: run the sweep on every push to develop (push events are not dropped) and keep the cron. Alternatives: a delayed self-dispatch, or a scheduler outside GitHub. If oracle-sweep-schedule-drops-most-runs-20261022, which has the same cron problem in oracle-verdict, has already chosen a shared mechanism, reuse it rather than building a second one.
2. Cost. Measure develop's push count over 7 days and the sweep's duration (about 2 minutes for 14 PRs on 2026-10-25). Record pushes times duration. If it exceeds 2 runner-hours a day, get the owner's approval before landing.
3. Concurrency. Back-to-back pushes must not pile up sweeps: give the sweep its own concurrency group that keeps the newest sweep, and never cancel per-PR gate runs. If the existing group layout makes that impossible without changing per-PR behaviour, stop and record why.

Item guardrails: no change to the gate decision, the statuses it posts, or how per-PR runs are triggered; the sweep remains the only multi-PR evaluator; no new secrets. oracle-gate.yml is a soundness path, so the PR needs the oracle's review.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests.
